note: THE TEXT ENCODED IS THE AS-INTRODUCED PRINT, AND IT HAS BEEN SUPERSEDED. The file held locally is named Bill+47-1.002.pdf, which on the Parliament's own bill page is the label for 'the Bill as passed by originating House'. It is not that text: its sha256 is byte-identical to the Internet Archive's 2025-12-31 capture of Bill+47-1.pdf, the as-introduced print, taken before the Legislative Assembly's Consideration in Detail on 2026-03-12. So either the local file was saved from the 'as Introduced' link under the other link's name, or the two links serve the same bytes. That cannot be settled from here: direct retrieval of Bill+47-1.002.pdf is refused by an Azure WAF JavaScript challenge, and the Internet Archive holds no capture of it. The consequence for every finding in INCIDENTS.md is recorded as entry EM-1 of the external-modifications register. Note also that local_path below is relative to THIS repository (legalese/canon), while the validator resolves local_path against the l4-ide repository root, so both digest rules report `skip` — incident H-07. The digests are `sha256sum` output and can be checked by hand.
in_force_absent_reason: A Bill has no in-force statement. This one is not law: as at 2026-09-23 it has passed the Legislative Assembly (third reading 2026-03-12) and been agreed at second reading in the Legislative Council (2026-09-15), with eleven Supplementary Notice Papers issued. Its commencement clause (s 2) provides for Part 1 on Royal Assent and the rest on proclamation, so even on assent the operative Parts would not be in force until proclaimed.

assembled.note: The artifact P3 encodes from: `pdftotext -layout` over the PDF, 3425 lines, 58 pages. Every quoted string in the L4 modules was taken from this file mechanically rather than retyped, which is the only reason the quotations in the encoding can be relied on.
